what: The KR venue<->bank real-name-account (실명확인 입출금계정) registry. Korean regulation binds each licensed VASP to EXACTLY ONE partner bank for KRW deposit/withdrawal. That makes every bank-level event a VENUE-ASYMMETRIC shock to one venue's fiat rail and not the other's -- an exogenous shifter of the intra-KR basis that is not a function of crypto price.
why_it_matters: R0299 wants an independent barrier-height regressor to break the KR-premium circularity. KR-s2 showed the intra-KR (Upbit-Bithumb) spread DIFFERENCES OUT the cross-border capital control that made kimchi ~73% artifact, because both legs sit behind the SAME control. What remains after that differencing is venue-specific, and the fiat rail is the largest venue-specific state variable there is. This file is the conditioning variable, not the signal.

regulatory_basis.rule: one exchange <-> one partner bank, exclusive
regulatory_basis.status_2026: STILL IN FORCE and under active political challenge -- Woori Bank's CEO publicly called for the single-bank rule to be lifted (2025-04). A repeal would END the asymmetry this axis rests on, so the axis carries a NAMED KILL CONDITION rather than an assumed persistence.

measured_events.measurement: Bithumb KRW-BTC 1m tape has a 10.50h HOLE: last bar 2025-03-23T15:30:00Z (00:30 KST 03-24), next bar 2025-03-24T02:00:00Z (11:00 KST). Price jumped +51bp across the halt. Upbit's 1m tape is CONTINUOUS through the same window (verified bar-by-bar).
measured_events.clock: venue-stamped candle_date_time_utc, both venues; verified aligned to the minute outside the gap
measured_events.why_recorded: the rail event is OBSERVABLE IN PRICE DATA AS AN ABSENCE. This is WS-011's confounder made concrete: the venue that halts is the venue with the rail event, so tape staleness is CORRELATED WITH THE TREATMENT and biases the event window specifically instead of averaging out.
measured_events.reproduce: GET https://api.bithumb.com/v1/candles/minutes/1?market=KRW-BTC&count=200&to=2025-03-24T13:00:00  (note: `to` is KST -- see the trap below)

THE_TRAP.name: bithumb `to` parameter is KST; upbit `to` is UTC
THE_TRAP.severity: silent -- no error, no gap, no warning; the returned candle_date_time_utc values are HONEST UTC and look perfectly normal, they are simply not the window you asked for
THE_TRAP.measured: asking both venues for to=2024-01-15T12:00:00 returns upbit 2024-01-15T11:59:00Z and bithumb 2024-01-15T02:59:00Z -- exactly 9h apart. Adding 9h to the bithumb request realigns them TO THE MINUTE (verified on 2024-01-15, 2020-03-13, 2018-01-11; the 4th test date failed only because it landed inside the 2025-03-24 outage above).
THE_TRAP.why_it_is_dangerous_here: data_axis_watchlist card #4 sells Bithumb as 'Upbit-SCHEMA-COMPATIBLE ... the desk's Upbit pagination code shape works'. That is TRUE of field names and pagination shape and FALSE of request-parameter semantics. A backfill loop written against Upbit and pointed at Bithumb walks a 9h-shifted window on EVERY call and compounds it across the whole paginated history.
THE_TRAP.separate_and_already_known: the DAILY bar boundary (upbit = UTC days, bithumb = KST days) is a DIFFERENT fact and the desk already killed it as `bithumb_kr_premium_lookahead` (docs/graveyard.md). This entry is about the REQUEST parameter, which that kill does not cover.
THE_TRAP.remedy: 1-MINUTE bars are honest UTC on both venues and align exactly once the +9h request offset is applied, so the intra-KR spread is constructible cleanly from 1m. The graveyard's framing reads as 'this venue is hazardous'; the measurement says 'this ENDPOINT is hazardous and the hazard is removable'.

history_depth_measured_2026-08-13.upbit_days: EMPTY [] before ~2017-10 (venue launch); to=2016-01-01 and to=2014-06-01 both return []
history_depth_measured_2026-08-13.bithumb_days: to=2016-01-01 -> 2015-12-30T15:00:00Z ; to=2014-06-01 -> 2014-05-15T15:00:00Z. Corroborates card #4's claim that Bithumb is the deeper free KRW archive.
history_depth_measured_2026-08-13.consequence: any intra-KR spread is bounded by the SHALLOWER leg (Upbit, ~2017-10), not by Bithumb's depth.

screen_status: NOT SCREENED -- and deliberately not, see below.
why_not_screened: The tradeable claim would be 'venue-asymmetric fiat rail state moves the intra-KR basis'. The desk has exactly ONE clean dated instance of the treatment (2025-03-24). n=1 is not an event study, it is an anecdote with a timestamp, and L1.62 forbids certifying a verdict on a sample size nobody measured. Running a screen on it would manufacture either a phantom edge or a false SCREEN-WEAK kill on a real one. The honest next step is to COUNT THE TREATMENT INSTANCES first (see next_step).
next_step: Enumerate the full set of KR venue<->bank rail transitions since 2018 (contract signings, renewals, migrations, terminations) from venue notice archives -- the desk already collects data/upbit_trade_announcements.jsonl (737 rows, 2017-10-27 ->) and Bithumb's feed.bithumb.com notice feed is catalogued on watchlist card #4. That converts n=1 into a countable event set, which is the precondition for a powered event study, not a substitute for one.
